kilde: OpenGrey (Institut de l'Information Scientifique et Technique)
sammendrag: In September 2001 the Pathfinder Extension program of innovative educational courses for adults was launched. An evaluation of the program was carried out and the brief for this overview report was to provide a concise, non-technical synthesis of findings. It offers interpretations of the findings which cut across the various parts of the evaluation. These interpretations are based on all the different kinds of evidence which the evaluation produced. The first section introduces the study and describes the parameters of the overview. The next two sections describe and place in context the Pathfinder Extension program and the evaluation. Section four describes what kinds of people came on the Extension programs, focusing particularly on what disadvantages or difficulties they faced, and explaining why these are important both for policy and for the evaluation. Section five talks about how the program was planned and delivered by the teachers, while section six tells how the courses were experienced by the learners, and also by employers. Section seven focuses on the primary question of the evaluation: Did the program make a difference to the education and employment outcomes of the participants compared with going on a traditional basic skills course? It describes the impacts of the program in terms of both education and employment. Finally, section eight sums up what has been learned from the evaluation. The Pathfinder Extension program reached more people with disadvantages in terms of ill-health and dyslexia and other learning difficulties. Both learners and teachers responded favourably to the Pathfinder Extension program indicating that there is a readiness to accept innovation in basic skills provision.
tittel: Evaluation of adult basic skills pathfinder extension activities: an overview
